title: Software Engineer
description:
PGS Worldwide is seeking a Software Engineer in Littleton, CO for a one-year contract-to-hire role supporting a leading aerospace & defense company.

The Software Engineer will support both backend and frontend software development in an Agile environment. This role requires hands-on experience with Java, JavaScript, or Python; modern web technologies; application containerization; cloud deployment; CI/CD pipelines; and frontend frameworks such as React, Angular, .NET, or Vue.js.

Required Skills

  • 4-year degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • 3+ years of hands-on software development experience.
  • Development experience with Java, JavaScript, or Python.
  • Backend and frontend software development experience.
  • HTML5, CSS3, and modern JavaScript experience.
  • Experience with frontend frameworks or libraries such as React, Angular, .NET, C#, or Vue.js.
  • Experience with state management tools such as Redux, NgRx, or Vuex.
  • Experience with application containerization tools such as Kubernetes, Helm, Docker, containers, or Containerd.
  • Experience deploying applications in cloud environments such as AWS, Azure, OpenStack, or OpenShift.
  • CI/CD experience, including deployment pipelines, automated builds, and configuration tools.
  • Agile development experience.
  • Experience using tools such as Jira and Confluence.
  • Familiarity with C#, .NET, or related technologies.
  • Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to communicate professionally, verbally and in writing.
  • Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, rapidly changing environment.
  • Strong time management skills and ability to support on-time project delivery.

Preferred Skills

  • Space domain experience.
  • Experience working in a collaborative software engineering environment.
  • Ability to build strong team relationships.
  • Experience delivering high-quality results in a mission-critical technical environment.
  • Aerospace, defense, cloud software, DevSecOps, or containerized application development experience.

What You’ll Do

  • Develop backend and frontend software applications.
  • Build and maintain software using Java, JavaScript, Python, C#, .NET, or related technologies.
  • Support modern web development using HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and frontend frameworks.
  • Develop and deploy containerized applications using tools such as Kubernetes, Helm, Docker, or Containerd.
  • Support cloud-based application deployment in AWS, Azure, OpenStack, OpenShift, or similar environments.
  • Work within CI/CD pipelines to support automated builds, deployments, and configuration management.
  • Participate in Agile development activities using tools such as Jira and Confluence.
  • Collaborate with technical teams to design, develop, test, and deliver software solutions.
  • Troubleshoot software issues and support continuous improvement.
  • Communicate technical status, risks, and progress clearly to team members and stakeholders.

title: AI/ML Research Engineer (Full-Stack, Agentic AI)
description:
PGS Worldwide is seeking an AI/ML Research Engineer (Full-Stack, Agentic AI) in a fully remote role for a one year contract-to-hire role supporting a leading aerospace & defense company. This role focuses on building agentic AI applications and AI assistant-style products using LLMs, Python, NLP, and enterprise-scale data platforms. You will develop and deploy scalable AI models, apply prompt engineering, and work with SQL and deep database technologies to deliver solutions aligned to project requirements in a fast-paced, collaborative environment.

Required Skills

  • Minimum 3 years of hands-on experience

  • 4-year degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Systems Engineering, or related field, or equivalent experience

  • Experience with agentic frameworks and building agentic AI applications

  • Strong proficiency in Python and prompt engineering for LLMs

  • Ability to differentiate between data models (e.g., Meta vs. OpenAI) based on project requirements

  • Hands-on experience with Natural Language Processing (NLP) and deploying scalable AI models

  • Deep knowledge of database technologies (SAP HANA, DB2, SQL Server) and strong SQL expertise

  • Experience building agentic AI or AI assistant-style products

  • Prior work with Lockheed Martin data platforms (EDE, LDW, EDW) or comparable enterprise-scale environments

  • Relevant cloud AI or machine learning certifications (e.g., Azure AI Engineer, AWS ML)

  • Ability to complete a vetting questionnaire (required for consideration)

Preferred Skills

  • Node.js

  • Predictive modeling

  • Knowledge/experience with Model Context Protocol (MCP)

  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, collaborative environment

What You’ll Do

  • Build agentic AI applications and AI assistant-style products using agentic frameworks and LLMs

  • Apply prompt engineering and Python development to deliver project-specific AI capabilities

  • Select and apply appropriate data/model approaches (e.g., Meta vs. OpenAI) based on project needs

  • Develop and deploy scalable NLP and AI/ML solutions in enterprise environments

  • Work with enterprise databases and data platforms using advanced SQL across SAP HANA, DB2, and SQL Server

  • Collaborate in a fast-paced team environment to deliver and iterate on AI solutions

title: HR Service Center Specialist
description:
PGS Worldwide is seeking an HR Service Center Specialist in Irving, TX for a one-year contract role supporting Northrop Grumman.

The HR Service Center Specialist will provide Tier 1 HR Help Desk support across phone, chat, email, and case management channels. This hybrid role requires HR shared services or call center experience, case management or ticketing system experience, strong Microsoft Office skills, and proficiency with AI-driven chatbots, voice assistants, and robotic process automation tools.

Required Skills

  • High school diploma or GED with relevant experience, or bachelor’s degree with 5+ years of relevant experience.
  • U.S. citizenship required.
  • HR shared services or call center experience.
  • Experience supporting high-volume employee, manager, HR partner, or stakeholder inquiries.
  • Experience using case management or ticketing systems in a high-volume support environment.
  • Proficiency with AI-driven chatbots, voice assistants, and robotic process automation solutions.
  • Advanced Microsoft Office skills, including Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and troubleshooting skills.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to manage sensitive, difficult, or complex interactions with professionalism and discretion.
  • Ability to document actions clearly and accurately in a case management system.
  • Ability to follow service-level agreements, company policies, data privacy standards, and regulatory requirements.
  • Ability to work a hybrid schedule in Irving, TX.

Preferred Skills

  • ServiceNow experience.
  • Workday experience.
  • HR shared services knowledge.
  • General payroll and timekeeping knowledge.
  • General travel and expense reporting knowledge.
  • Experience supporting HR policy, payroll, benefits, compliance, timekeeping, travel and expense, or employee lifecycle inquiries.
  • Continuous improvement experience.
  • Experience using automation or AI tools to streamline HR workflows.

What You’ll Do

  • Provide Tier 1 HR Help Desk support across phone, chat, email, and case management channels.
  • Respond to inquiries from employees, managers, HR partners, and external stakeholders.
  • Support HR, payroll, timekeeping, travel and expense, and employee lifecycle inquiries.
  • Use knowledge-based resources, troubleshooting techniques, and AI-assisted tools to resolve issues.
  • Document support actions clearly in the case management system.
  • Manage difficult interactions while maintaining professionalism and customer satisfaction.
  • Escalate complex or sensitive issues when appropriate.
  • Complete back-office HR tasks such as employment verifications, document management, PTO donations, mail processing, W-4 updates, workplace accommodations, and emergency contact activation.
  • Maintain compliance with company policies, data privacy standards, and employee information requirements.
  • Collaborate with internal stakeholders and cross-functional teams to improve service delivery.
  • Participate in process improvement initiatives involving AI-driven chatbots, voice assistants, and robotic process automation.
  • Continue building technical and functional HR support expertise.

Work Schedule / Shift

  • Monday–Friday, 5x8 schedule.
  • Must be available during operating hours of 7:00 AM–6:00 PM CST.
  • Hybrid schedule: in office Tuesday and Wednesday; remote Monday, Thursday, and Friday.
  • Hybrid schedule may be subject to change.
  • Full-time, 40 hours per week.
  • No travel required.

Pay

  • $26.47/hour

title: ESS Test Technician
description:
PGS Worldwide is seeking an ESS Test Technician in Austin, TX for a temp-to-hire role supporting a leading aerospace & defense company.

The ESS Test Technician will perform environmental stress screening and operational testing on complex electronic production components and subassemblies. This 1st shift role requires hands-on vibration systems experience, vibration profile development experience, environmental test setup experience, and the ability to process and compile complete test data packages.

Required Skills

  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • U.S. citizenship required.
  • 1+ year of experience performing operational tests on complex electronic production components or subassemblies.
  • 1+ year of direct experience working with Unholtz-Dickie or similar vibration systems.
  • 1+ year of vibration profile development experience.
  • Experience supporting engineering qualification or environmental test efforts.
  • Experience setting up and operating vibration systems and thermal cycling equipment.
  • Experience with Thermotron temperature chambers.
  • Ability to conduct environmental tests involving temperature and vibration.
  • Ability to follow standard test methods, procedures, engineering instructions, and verbal instructions.
  • Basic computer skills in a Microsoft Windows environment.
  • Ability to maintain test logbooks with accurate test information.
  • Ability to process and compile product data, quality information, and defect records.
  • Ability to work independently and in a team environment.
  • Strong attention to detail and documentation accuracy.

Preferred Skills

  • Experience with thermocouples, data loggers, vibration controls, accelerometer systems, pressure instrumentation, or air flow instrumentation.
  • Experience using test and measurement equipment such as automated test equipment, oscilloscopes, digital multimeters, logic analyzers, or other electronic instrumentation.
  • Experience supporting environmental stress screening, engineering qualification testing, electronics testing, or production test environments.
  • Experience assisting higher-level technicians with complex test activities.
  • Aerospace, defense, electronics manufacturing, or high-reliability production experience.

What You'll Do

  • Perform operational testing on complex electronic production components and subassemblies.
  • Support Environmental Stress Screening testing for production and engineering groups.
  • Set up and operate vibration systems and thermal cycling equipment.
  • Conduct simulated environmental testing involving temperature and vibration.
  • Use monitoring and control equipment such as thermocouples, data loggers, vibration controls, accelerometer systems, and related instrumentation.
  • Support testing using automated test equipment and individual electronic test instruments.
  • Follow standard test methods, engineering procedures, written instructions, and verbal direction.
  • Assist higher-classified technicians with more complex test activities.
  • Process and compile product test data into complete data packages.
  • Record quality information and defect data.
  • Maintain test logbooks with accurate and complete test information.
  • Perform other test support duties as assigned.

Work Schedule / Shift

  • 1st shift.
  • Monday–Thursday, 4/10 schedule.
  • Typical hours are 6:00 AM–4:30 PM.
  • Full-time, 40 hours per week.
  • No overtime expected.
  • No travel required.

Pay

  • $22.86/hour

title: Electronic Assembler
description:
PGS Worldwide is seeking an Electronic Assembler in Austin, TX for a temporary contract role supporting a leading aerospace & defense company.

The Electronic Assembler will support onsite production assembly of advanced electronic and electromechanical assemblies. This 2nd shift role requires hand soldering experience, rework experience, mechanical assembly or tack bonding experience, the ability to read drawings and work instructions, and comfort working in a clean room production environment.

Required Skills

  • High school or trade school education.
  • U.S. citizenship required.
  • Hand soldering experience required.
  • Rework experience.
  • Mechanical assembly and/or tack bonding/epoxy experience.
  • Ability to read and interpret work instructions, schematics, blueprints, process plans, and drawings.
  • Ability to assemble parts for electromechanical equipment.
  • Ability to manually solder or epoxy electrical components.
  • Ability to inspect parts and materials for flaws and imperfections before use.
  • Ability to assemble, disassemble, and modify production subassemblies by following work plans.
  • Ability to inspect completed work for conformance.
  • Ability to become solder certified.
  • Basic computer skills.
  • Microsoft Office familiarity, including Excel, Word, and Outlook.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong attention to detail, accuracy, teamwork, and work ethic.
  • Ability to work 100% onsite in Austin, TX.
  • Ability to work 2nd shift on a 4/10 schedule.

Preferred Skills

  • IPC Class 3 soldering, connector installation, and epoxy application experience.
  • J-STD modules 1, 3, and 6 completed.
  • IPC-A-610 certification.
  • J-STD-001 certification.
  • Selective solder experience.
  • High-volume wave soldering experience.
  • AOI and AXI/X-ray inspection experience.
  • IPC-A-610 and J-STD-001 inspection experience.
  • Experience using fixturing to accurately build assemblies.
  • Experience using solder reflow ovens, semi-automatic pick-and-place machines, or automated measurement systems.
  • MRP or data collection software experience.
  • Clean room experience.
  • Willingness to learn new technologies and adapt to changing production environments.

What You'll Do

  • Assemble electronic and electromechanical production hardware.
  • Perform hand soldering, connector installation, rework, and epoxy/tack bonding.
  • Read and follow work instructions, drawings, schematics, blueprints, and process plans.
  • Assemble, disassemble, and modify production subassemblies.
  • Inspect parts, materials, and completed assemblies for conformance.
  • Use fixturing, soldering tools, reflow ovens, semi-automatic pick-and-place equipment, and automated measurement systems as applicable.
  • Support production accuracy, quality, and schedule requirements.
  • Work independently and as part of a production team.
  • Maintain quality standards in a clean room manufacturing environment.

Work Schedule / Shift

  • 2nd shift.
  • Monday–Thursday, 4/10 schedule.
  • Typical hours are 4:30 PM–3:00 AM.
  • Full-time, 40 hours per week.
  • Overtime expected as needed.
  • 100% onsite role.
  • No travel required.

Pay

  • $24.19/hour base pay for candidates without industry experience.
  • $27.00/hour base pay for candidates with industry experience.
  • Shift differential may apply.

title: Secret-Cleared Embedded Software Engineer
description:
PGS Worldwide is seeking a Secret-Cleared Embedded Software Engineer in Chandler, AZ for a one-year contract role supporting Northrop Grumman.

The Embedded Software Engineer will support Launch Systems programs by developing, debugging, testing, integrating, and maintaining real-time embedded software. This onsite role requires C/C++ object-oriented software development experience in a Linux environment, embedded real-time software experience, RTOS experience, full software development lifecycle experience, and an active DoD Secret clearance investigated within the last 5 years.

Required Skills

  • Bachelor of Science or Engineering degree in Computer Science, Computer Systems, or a related discipline.
  • U.S. citizenship required.
  • Active DoD Secret security clearance investigated within the last 5 years.
  • Object-oriented software development experience in C/C++.
  • Linux development experience.
  • Embedded real-time software development, debugging, and testing experience.
  • Real-time operating system experience, such as VxWorks, Integrity, LynxOS, Yocto Linux, or equivalent RTOS.
  • Full software development lifecycle experience.
  • Ability to support requirements development, architecture development, detailed design, coding, unit testing, integration, and test.
  • Strong problem-solving and troubleshooting skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work in a collaborative, multi-disciplinary team environment.
  • Ability to work onsite in Chandler, AZ.

Preferred Skills

  • Experience with PowerPC, ARM, and/or RISC-V architectures.
  • Experience with real-time computer-in-the-loop or hardware-in-the-loop test laboratories.
  • Experience developing interfaces to support weapon system integration.
  • Launch vehicle, missile defense, aerospace, defense, or mission-critical embedded software experience.

What You’ll Do

  • Develop embedded real-time software for Launch Systems programs.
  • Support requirements development, software architecture, detailed design, coding, unit testing, integration, and test.
  • Develop software in C/C++ within a Linux environment.
  • Debug and test embedded real-time software.
  • Work with RTOS environments such as VxWorks, Integrity, LynxOS, Yocto Linux, or equivalent systems.
  • Ensure software standards are met.
  • Support integration and testing activities for real-time embedded systems.
  • Collaborate with multi-disciplinary engineering teams.
  • Troubleshoot software issues and support technical problem resolution.
  • Support weapon system integration efforts as needed.

Work Schedule / Shift

  • 9x80 A schedule.
  • Full-time, 40 hours per week.
  • Onsite role.

Pay

  • $90.00/hour

title: Manufacturing Equipment Technician
description:
PGS Worldwide is seeking a Manufacturing Equipment Technician in Oldsmar, FL for a one-year contract-to-hire role supporting a leading aerospace & defense company.

The Manufacturing Equipment Technician will install, maintain, troubleshoot, repair, and improve manufacturing equipment used in circuit card assembly production. This 1st shift role requires strong SMT equipment experience, AOI experience, electronics troubleshooting ability, mechanical aptitude, and at least 10 years of related technical experience.

Required Skills

  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • 10+ years of related technical, manufacturing equipment, maintenance, repair, or para-engineering experience.
  • SMT manufacturing equipment experience.
  • AOI equipment experience.
  • Ability to read and write English.
  • General knowledge of mechanical hand tools and soldering equipment.
  • Working knowledge of electronics, pneumatics, hydraulics, and mechanical systems.
  • Ability to troubleshoot manufacturing equipment using drawings, diagrams, sketches, specifications, prints, manuals, and written or verbal instructions.
  • Ability to locate failures and replace defective components or modules.
  • Experience performing preventative and corrective maintenance on production equipment.
  • Strong problem-solving skills related to process, product, equipment, and procedure issues.
  • Ability to maintain maintenance, inventory, and repair logs.
  • Ability to use hand tools, power tools, test tools, and related equipment.
  • Ability to work with or around chemicals used in production areas.
  • Ability to support a flexible schedule, including possible weekend work or first/second shift coverage.
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills.
  • Ability to complete required manufacturing training programs, including PWB handling, first piece certification, component identification, and ESD.

Preferred Skills

  • Associate degree or vocational certificate in a technical program.
  • Bachelor’s degree.
  • MyCronic pick-and-place experience.
  • Universal Instruments pick-and-place experience.
  • Koh Young or YesTech AOI experience.
  • SMT circuit card assembly inline wash experience.
  • MPM screen printer experience.
  • Experience supporting circuit card assembly production.
  • Experience working with production leadership, product engineering, process engineering, quality engineering, or test engineering teams.

What You’ll Do

  • Install, maintain, troubleshoot, and repair in-line manufacturing equipment.
  • Monitor, evaluate, report, and improve manufacturing equipment performance.
  • Perform preventative and corrective maintenance on CCA production equipment.
  • Complete immediate repairs to reduce equipment downtime.
  • Diagnose failures and replace defective components or modules.
  • Perform basic troubleshooting using standard electronic equipment and technical documentation.
  • Support improvements to optical, vacuum, electrical, electronic, or mechanical systems on existing equipment.
  • Maintain accurate maintenance, inventory, and repair logs.
  • Use hand tools, power tools, test tools, and equipment to support repairs and maintenance.
  • Work with production line leadership, product engineers, process engineers, quality engineers, and test engineers.
  • Estimate labor or equipment needs and support requisitions as required.
  • Support production requirements through flexible shift or weekend coverage as needed.

Work Schedule / Shift

  • 1st shift.
  • Monday–Thursday, 5:00 AM–3:30 PM.
  • Flexible schedule may be required, including possible weekend work or first/second shift coverage.
  • Overtime expected as needed.

Pay

  • $26.00–$35.00/hour

title: Conformal Coating Assembler
description:
PGS Worldwide is seeking a Conformal Coating Assembler in Oldsmar, FL for a one-year contract-to-hire role supporting a leading aerospace & defense company.

The Conformal Coating Assembler will operate dispensing and coating equipment, mask and tape circuit boards, inspect coating coverage, perform manual touch-up, and support potting, bonding, coating, encapsulation, and finishing processes for electronic assemblies. This 1st shift role requires attention to detail, the ability to read and write English, and the ability to pass a required medical exam.

Required Skills

  • Assembly, coating, paint process, manufacturing, or electronic production experience.
  • Ability to read and write English.
  • Ability to pass a required medical exam.
  • Ability to operate dispensing and coating machines.
  • Ability to mask and tape circuit boards in areas that must remain free of conformal coating or potting.
  • Ability to inspect assemblies for proper coating coverage.
  • Ability to remove excess coating and perform manual touch-up.
  • Ability to work with chemicals, solvents, compounds, process fluids, coatings, bonding materials, and potting materials.
  • Ability to follow customer specifications, work instructions, and safety requirements.
  • Ability to transport racks of circuit boards throughout the manufacturing process.
  • Ability to perform general housekeeping to maintain a safe and clean work area.

Preferred Skills

  • Conformal coating experience.
  • Potting, bonding, encapsulation, or finishing process experience.
  • Paint process, paint systems, or coating materials experience.
  • Basic computer skills.
  • Experience maintaining coating, dispensing, or production equipment.
  • Experience replenishing chemicals, solvents, compounds, or process fluids.
  • Experience working with circuit boards, electronic assemblies, or high-reliability manufacturing.

What You’ll Do

  • Operate dispensing and coating machines to meet customer specifications.
  • Mask and tape circuit boards before coating or potting.
  • Inspect assemblies to confirm proper coating coverage.
  • Remove excess coating and manually touch up missed areas.
  • Maintain coating and dispensing machines in proper operating condition.
  • Change fluids and mixers and clean machines as needed.
  • Encapsulate discrete assemblies.
  • Prepare and apply potting, bonding, coating compounds, lubricants, spray coats, or insulated tape to components and assemblies.
  • Replenish chemicals, solvents, compounds, and process fluids as required.
  • Dispense materials into secondary containers and perform chemical cleaning.
  • Transport product, material, tools, and circuit board racks throughout the manufacturing process.
  • Complete applicable specific function training courses.
  • Support additional production tasks as assigned by the supervisor.

Work Schedule / Shift

  • 1st shift.
  • Monday–Thursday, 5:00 AM–3:30 PM.
  • Full-time schedule.
  • Overtime expected as needed.

Pay

  • $20.00–$25.00/hour

title: Dimension Control Technician
description:
PGS Worldwide is seeking a Secret-Eligible Dimension Control Technician in Palmdale, CA for a 6-month contract-to-hire role supporting Northrop Grumman.

The Dimension Control Technician will support fabrication, assembly, alignment, inspection, maintenance, and repair of aerospace jigs and fixtures used in aircraft manufacturing. This onsite role requires hands-on experience with CMM, CNC, machining, or laser tracking, aerospace tooling knowledge, metrology experience, and the ability to obtain and maintain a DoD Secret clearance, including Special Access Program access.

Required Skills

  • High school diploma, GED, or equivalent.
  • 4+ years of related experience.
  • U.S. citizenship required.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a DoD Secret clearance, including Special Access Program access.
  • Experience with CMM, CNC, machining, and/or laser tracking.
  • Aerospace tooling experience.
  • Knowledge of metrology processes, including setting details with a laser tracker.
  • Ability to interpret engineering drawings, blueprints, and schematics.
  • Ability to fabricate, assemble, align, inspect, maintain, and repair jigs and fixtures.
  • Experience using precision measuring tools such as calipers, micrometers, or laser measuring systems.
  • Ability to lift, move, push, or pull 35–50 lbs. throughout the workday.
  • Ability to work inside and outside in a warehouse or shop floor environment.
  • Ability to handle and assemble small parts and machinery.
  • Ability to work any assigned shift as needed.
  • Ability to travel as needed.

Preferred Skills

  • Associate degree.
  • Laser tracking experience with assembly tools in an aircraft manufacturing environment.
  • Forklift operation experience.
  • Overhead crane operation experience.
  • Tool and die making or related experience.
  • 3D CAD experience.
  • Siemens NX, CATIA, or applicable 3D CAD system experience.
  • Experience with computer-aided metrology systems such as laser trackers, articulated arms, scanners, or 6DoF systems.
  • Experience with Verisurf, SpatialAnalyzer, Maya matrix, BuildIT, or PolyWorks.
  • Experience analyzing collected data against computer models.
  • Knowledge of integrated systems airframes and aero structures.
  • Experience creating working build models in Verisurf or related software.

What You’ll Do

  • Fabricate and assemble jigs and fixtures used in aerospace manufacturing.
  • Interpret engineering drawings, blueprints, and schematics.
  • View and support jig and fixture design using CAD software.
  • Fabricate tooling using materials such as aluminum, steel, or composites.
  • Assemble jigs and fixtures and verify proper alignment.
  • Use precision measuring tools and laser measuring systems to confirm dimensions.
  • Adjust and fine-tune tooling to meet accuracy and precision requirements.
  • Inspect jigs and fixtures for quality, compliance, and customer specifications.
  • Document inspection results, adjustments, and maintenance activity.
  • Perform routine maintenance, cleaning, lubrication, and part replacement on tooling.
  • Identify and repair damaged or worn jig and fixture components.
  • Collaborate with engineers, machinists, quality personnel, and production teams.
  • Support continuous improvement efforts to improve tooling performance and manufacturing efficiency.

Work Schedule / Shift

  • 4x10 schedule.
  • Full-time, 40 hours per week.
  • Onsite role.
  • Must be able to work any shift as needed.
  • Travel may be required.

Pay

  • $39.59/hour

title: Mechanical Engineer
description:
PGS Worldwide is seeking a Mechanical Engineer in Merrimack, NH for a temporary contract role supporting a leading aerospace & defense company.

The Mechanical Engineer will support structural and thermal analysis for circuit card assemblies, electronic chassis structures, and related mechanical hardware. This role requires NASTRAN experience, structural analysis capability, thermal modeling experience, and the ability to independently execute analysis tasks, document results, and provide design recommendations.

Required Skills

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or a closely related field from an ABET-accredited institution.
  • U.S. citizenship required.
  • Structural and thermal analysis experience with mechanical components or electronic hardware.
  • NASTRAN experience for structural analysis.
  • Ability to perform vibration, shock, static, and fatigue analyses.
  • Ability to perform thermal modeling and assessments.
  • Experience with random vibration, shock, fatigue, and static loading analyses.
  • Ability to independently execute analysis tasks and reporting.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to clearly document and present technical results.
  • Strong communication skills for interfacing with design teams.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal oversight.

Preferred Skills

  • Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering or related discipline.
  • 8–10 years of relevant experience.
  • Experience with circuit card assemblies and electronic chassis structures.
  • Experience with Icepak for CCA thermal analysis.
  • Experience using Simcenter 3D for system-level structural and thermal modeling.
  • Exposure to pressure drop or coolant flow analysis, including cold plates.
  • Experience analyzing solder joint reliability, including low-cycle and high-cycle fatigue.
  • Acoustic loading analysis experience.
  • System-level analysis experience for electronic assemblies.
  • Thermal and flow analysis experience for cooling solutions.

What You'll Do

  • Perform structural and thermal analysis for mechanical components and electronic hardware.
  • Support analysis of circuit card assemblies and chassis structures.
  • Perform structural, vibration, shock, fatigue, static, and thermal assessments.
  • Generate analysis models to support design teams.
  • Document analysis results and present technical findings.
  • Provide design recommendations based on analysis results.
  • Support system-level structural and thermal modeling.
  • Evaluate loading conditions, reliability concerns, and cooling-related design factors.
  • Work independently with minimal oversight while coordinating with design teams.

Work Schedule / Shift

  • 1st shift.
  • Monday–Friday.
  • 9/80 schedule.
  • Typical hours are 8:00 AM–4:30 PM.
  • Full-time, 40 hours per week.
  • Overtime expected as needed.
  • No travel required.

Pay

  • $63.50/hour

Job ID: 7536

Military veterans and transitioning military members are encouraged to apply to all PGS Worldwide positions. All of our jobs are military-friendly, and we work with leaders in Aerospace who rely on your military expertise to support mission-critical programs nationwide. As a Veteran Founded company, we know that the military has given you the skills and training you need to succeed in positions like this, and we want to support your success in the civilian sector however we can. We thank you for your service and humbly offer our own in return by helping you take your career to the next level.
